titleEn: Well Water Flows, Hands Scrub Clean!

pages.text: "I want bread!" Lulu grabbed some at the yard table. Black field soil covered the fingertips. A brown handprint marked the white tablecloth.
"I can wash later! Bread first!" Lulu took a big bite, cheeks bulging. The cousins were already washing at the well.
Gurgle! Lulu curled up with both hands on the tummy. Long ears lay back, tears gathering. "Ow... My tummy aches."
Mom held Lulu's back and walked to the yard well. "Field soil carries things we cannot see. They got on the bread and into your tummy." Lulu lowered the head. "I did not see them..."
Mom pointed to the brown handprint. "Dirty hands leave marks like this. What about clean hands?" No marks by the cousins' seats.
Mom drew water from the well. Splash! "One, catch water from the bucket! Two, soap bubbles! Three, rinse between your fingers!" Lulu held both blunt hands under it.
Lulu rubbed both hands together, interlacing three fingers. White foam covered them, and water ran below the wrists. "Well water flows, hands scrub clean!"
Lulu dried both hands on the towel over one shoulder. Now they looked as bright as Lulu's face. The tummy settled too. A clap, and the blue bell jingled.

Next day, when snack bread arrived, Lulu led to the well, raising a forepaw with three fingers spread. "Hands before bread! One, water! Two, bubbles! Three, between the fingers!" The cousins followed.
Mom hugged Lulu. Wash before eating, and your tummy is comfortable and the tablecloth white. "Look, no marks! Well water flows, hands scrub clean!"
